name: Violet-Core Physique
reason: Source term 'Extreme Purple Yin Body' (also rendered 'Extreme Violet Yin Body' in the translation) was localized as 'Violet-Core Physique' to fit the Western fantasy register while keeping the violet color motif.
description: A rare special constitution found only in certain maidens; both Elara and Marilyn possess a Violet-Core Physique. It is highly coveted by hostile powers (in the source it is required for the Heavenly Devil Joyous Union Formation), making its bearers targets, and the Cobalt Dragon repeatedly ties major plot threads back to Elara's physique.

name: Brent
reason: The character's Chinese name 'Xiao Jie' was fully localized to the US-origin name 'Brent', a short, confident name fitting the brash young prodigy archetype.
description: An Ethereal Spirit Sect disciple and the youngest competitor (15) in the grand tournament arc, with Saint-level talent and Peak Soul Realm cultivation. Hailed as the most talented genius in the region's history, he had already grasped half of Spatial Law and was eager to challenge Zane. He remains on friendly terms with Zane, who later visits the Ethereal Spirit Sect to say goodbye to him.

name: Spirit Weapon
issues: Ep 4 mistakenly used 'Soul Armament' for this tier (per master sheet); 'Soul Armament' is separately the name of Zane's body-weapon, so the two must not be conflated.
reason: Source term 'Spiritual Weapon' was localized as 'Spirit Weapon', keeping the canonical weapon-tier naming of the adaptation (Tier 2 on the master sheet).
description: A canonical weapon classification in the show's armament tier system (listed as Tier 2 on the master sheet, alongside Mysterious, Mythic, Sacred Arms and Divine Arms). Spirit Weapons are treated as rarer and more precious than ordinary Mythic weapons in forging contexts; shops and vaults stock them as prized treasures, and forging one marks a weaponsmith's mastery.

name: God
reason: Generic exclamation and common noun ('God, we're screwed', 'Oh my God', generic gods/deities), not a trackable localized entity.

name: James Moon
reason: The character's Chinese name 'Mo Xiuyan' was fully localized to 'James Moon'; the surname 'Moon' renders the Mo family as House Moon to keep a consistent family unit.
description: Head of House Moon (source: head of the Mo family and its only Divine Reflection Realm expert), a Soul Realm master, Yates's father and Ethan's uncle. He stole the Bloodstone Bracelet (source: the Mixed Blood Bracelet carved from Mixed Yuan Blood Jade) from Ethan's deceased father, and is publicly humiliated by Zane at his own gathering in Eps 197-204.

name: Lucky Light
reason: Source term 'Light of Good Fortune' was localized as the punchier 'Lucky Light' for the Western fantasy setting.
description: A reward energy of the Tower of Sin arena system on the Sea God Continent: defeating an opponent grants a portion of Lucky Light, which flows into the victor (and his token) and directly strengthens cultivation. Zane farms it alongside Malice during the arena arc (Eps 432+ and 570s) to accelerate his growth.

name: Shattered Dagger
reason: Source term 'broken Flying Dagger', Luo Zheng's signature early weapon, was localized as 'Shattered Dagger' to preserve the broken-blade image in a Western register.
description: Zane's signature weapon through the early and middle episodes: a telekinetically guided dagger of extraordinary sharpness that he hurls and steers remotely, able to tear through soil and stone and strike from unexpected angles. The master sheet notes it is sometimes called simply 'the dagger' in narration, which is acceptable.

name: Cloudhaven
reason: Source city 'Ocean of Clouds City' (also translated 'Cloud Sea City') was localized as 'Cloudhaven' to fit the Western fantasy register while keeping the cloud motif.
description: The mortal city lying far below the floating fortress of Cloud Hall, home to the Cloud School and a branch of the World Merchants' Guild. Its fate is tied to Cloud Hall's: when Maddox's arrival loomed, dread settled over both the fortress above and Cloudhaven below.

name: War King Wind
reason: Source title-name 'Tianfeng War Emperor' (Tianfeng = 'Heavenly Wind') was localized as 'War King Wind', keeping the wind element of his kingdom's name.
description: Monarch of one of the four Divine Kingdoms and a Soul Sea Realm powerhouse, one of the supreme rulers who preside over the great tournament (Eps 814+). He is a doting father: when his daughter was endangered in the arena he shattered the enchanted barrier without hesitation and yanked her to safety (source: the Tianfeng War Emperor pulling Huo Yuner from the barrier). He watches Zane's rise with a mix of awe and heavy-hearted resignation, and ascends to the Upper World near Ep 1001.

name: Marrow Refining Level
reason: Source cultivation stage 'Marrow Refining Stage' (also 'Marrow Refining Realm') was kept nearly literal as 'Marrow Refining Level', matching the show's 'Level' naming for body-cultivation stages.
description: An advanced body-cultivation stage in the early system, following the Bone and Organ refining stages and paired with the Core Strength Level as the final tiers before the Nature Level. Early-arc fights frequently measure strength against it, as when Zane holds his own against four Marrow Refining Level opponents.

name: Tristan
issues: Name collision: 'Tristan' refers to TWO different characters - the antagonist Tristan Hayes (Eps 54-58, dies at Ep 58) and this young House Lowell member (Eps 324-329). This dossier's mention stats merge both; do not alias to Tristan Hayes.
reason: A US-origin first name assigned to a minor House Lowell (source: Luo Family) junior for the family-return arc.
description: A young House Lowell member with 'no real standing in the family', found punished and in pain when Zane returns home in disguise (Ep 324). He finds his courage and sides with Zane against Bryson Lowell, invoking their shared family name even with Bryson's sword at his throat (Eps 326-329).

name: Tristan Hayes
issues: Shares the first name 'Tristan' with an unrelated House Lowell character in Eps 324-329; the two must remain separate entities.
reason: The character's Chinese name 'Xu Lie' was fully localized to 'Tristan Hayes', a complete US-style name for the early arena antagonist.
description: An early antagonist (Eps 54-58) who fought Zane in the sect arena using the Indigo Blade borrowed from Julian Croft (source: Xu Lie wielding the Zi Qing Treasure Sword lent by He Bing). He is defeated at Ep 58, the lightning around him fading as his life force drains away.

name: Livingston
reason: Source moniker 'Lian Shenzi' (rendered 'Refined Shenzi' in the translation, roughly 'Master of Refining') was localized to the distinguished-sounding Western name 'Livingston' fitting his self-styled master-craftsman persona.
description: A clanking old puppet who proclaims himself 'the number one weaponsmith in the universe', encountered in the late arc (Eps 1153+). Though younger warriors have never heard his name, his title carries weight; having lived as a puppet for ages, he guards and spills dangerous crafting secrets. Zane bags him at the first opportunity to keep him from talking to the wrong people (source: Luo Zheng stuffing Refined Shenzi into his Spirit Beast Pouch).

name: Dorian Sinclair
reason: The character's Chinese name 'Situ Haotian' was fully localized to 'Dorian Sinclair'; his Purple Heart Sacred Land was correspondingly renamed the Violet Heart Sanctuary.
description: Head of the Violet Heart Sanctuary (source: Situ Haotian of the Purple Heart Sacred Land / Holy Land). A measured leader who weathers defections during the faction conflicts of Eps 628+, he recognizes Zane's limitless potential, treats him with marked respect, and knows better than to try to force him to stay.

name: Jace
reason: The character's Chinese name 'Xie Lang' was fully localized to 'Jace' (styled 'Evil Jace' on the master sheet), a short, sharp name for the manic rogue weaponsmith.
description: A rogue weaponsmith and early antagonist (Eps 19-25), creator of the Hellfire Blade (source: Xie Lang, the evil weapon refiner of Chongyang County who hid inside his copper furnace). Far beyond Zane's league at the time, he cackles through their deadly confrontation; Zane later studies the Advanced Forging texts Jace left behind.

name: Point
reason: The source sect's contribution 'points' were kept as 'Points' (also 'Sect Points'), the sect-internal merit currency of the adaptation.
description: The sect's merit currency, earned by disciples through missions and tasks and spent on techniques and resources; a hundred Points had a market value of about two hundred Crystal Cubes. Distinct from the later 'Nexus Points' body-refining term on the master sheet.

name: Nature Level
reason: Source cultivation stage 'Xiantian Realm' (Innate Realm) was localized as 'Nature Level', echoing the 'innate/natural' sense of the Chinese term.
description: The elite cultivation stage above the Marrow Refining and Core Strength Levels in the early system, at which cultivators use 'Life Force' rather than 'Life Energy' per the show's canon. Early arcs track Zane's progress as 'half a step into the Nature Level' (source: Half-step Xiantian Realm), and stages within it are ranked (e.g. rank six).

name: Aurora
issues: Gender mismatch: episodes portray Aurora as female ('her pale blue eyes', f16 pronoun signal), but the source character Aizen is male ('Lord Aizen', 'his face'). Also a split entity: in Eps 223-224 'Aurora' is a natural light phenomenon used for sword-intent training, unrelated to this character; those mentions are folded into this dossier.
reason: Source name 'Aizen' was localized as 'Aurora'; the adaptation also presents the character as female, diverging from the male source character.
description: A leader figure in the Illusion Battlefield arc (Eps 1246+) whom followers like Rowan serve and come to help (source: 'I came here to help Lord Aizen' in the Toona Divine Tree sequence). Wary of the unknown Zane, Aurora watches him with pale blue eyes, fingers trembling on the edge of an attack, and can compensate followers' lost Illusion Points.

name: Toby Dillon
reason: The character's Chinese name 'Elder Fei Han' was fully localized to 'Toby Dillon', a complete US-style name for the Cloud Hall elder overseeing the trials.
description: A Cloud Hall elder with senior authority over all sect stewards during the Cloud Road / Road of Trials arc (Eps 357+). He opens the Cloud Road gateway, watches the competing disciples through a Scrying Slate, and initially favors Zane, offering him the coveted Nimbus Expanse Pill as a political maneuver, though per the master sheet he grows envious and hostile toward Zane over time.

name: Time Law
reason: Source term 'Law of Time' was localized as 'Time Law', matching the show's compact 'X Law' naming for the laws.
description: One of the two foundational laws of the Upper World alongside Spatial Law, and among the most mysterious of all laws. Mastery lets a warrior alter the flow of time - slowing opponents, locking them in place, or gaining extra cultivation hours from time-infused artifacts - making it nearly unanswerable by speed or technique alone.

name: Law Power
reason: Source term 'Power of Law' (also 'Law Power' in the translation) was localized as 'Law Power' for the Western fantasy register.
description: The fundamental energy of comprehended laws (fire, wind, thunder, space, time and others) that Upper World warriors study, typically deciphered from inscriptions on obelisks over decades. It is graded in levels, and advanced martial arts require blending two or three types of Law Power and switching between them; a natural affinity for it is what Upper World scouts seek in Lower World talents.

name: Razorwing
reason: Source creature 'Saber Insect' (also translated 'Blade Insect') was localized as 'Razorwing', a vivid Western monster name preserving the blade imagery.
description: Ferocious swarm beasts hunted during the trial arc (Eps 61-97): creatures that live to kill, deceptively strong individually and deadly in swarms led by Alphas and commanders. Their monster cores are valuable - Zane amasses thousands of regular cores and hundreds of commander cores to trade for Points.

name: Razorwing Queen
reason: Source creature 'Saber Insect Queen' (also 'Blade Insect Queen') was localized as 'Razorwing Queen', consistent with the Razorwing race rename.
description: The monstrous apex ruler of the Razorwing swarms, a sixty-to-seventy-foot horror whose shriek alone is a physical assault. It kills Rex with a single strike, squares off against the Scorpiomane as a fellow apex predator, and the trial survivors owe their lives to Zane drawing it away (Eps 67-97).

name: Larkin
reason: The character's Chinese name 'Jin Hai' was fully localized to 'Larkin', a US-origin name for the elusive hook-wielder of the Karma Hall arc.
description: A cautious, calculating hook-wielder in the Karma Hall standoff (Eps 1276-1286), speaking from the darkness beside Damon and refusing to be lured across to Zane (source: Jin Hai, who hides within his own conjured fog and disarms prodigies with hooks bearing Heavenly Dao / Karma Law power). Intrigued by Zane, he studies his own hook and hesitates until Zane finally sends a hook at his blurred outline in the dark.

name: War Emperor York
issues: Master sheet lists an unrelated minor opponent 'York' of Sea Peak at Ep 240; that is a different character and should not be merged with War Emperor York.
reason: Source title-name 'Battle Emperor Yu the Great' of the Great Yu Divine Kingdom was localized as 'War Emperor York', with 'York' standing in for 'Yu' as the kingdom's name.
description: Monarch of the York Divine Kingdom (source: Great Yu Divine Kingdom) and one of the four Divine Kingdom rulers at the Soul Sea Realm, long stuck at the threshold of the Divine Sea Realm. He possesses the Eyes of the Darkest Night, presides sternly over the great tournament (Eps 800+), and is repeatedly stunned and angered by Zane's impossible feats; he is Fredrick's sovereign and ascends to the Upper World around Ep 1001.

name: Fredrick
reason: The character's Chinese name 'Liu Xiu' was fully localized to 'Fredrick', a princely US-origin name fitting the crown prince archetype.
description: Crown prince of the York Divine Kingdom (source: Liu Xiu, Crown Prince of the Great Yu Divine Kingdom), who gets priority access to his kingdom's treasures from the Reverse Spirit Channel. He skipped the previous tournament and carries a hidden talent that is 'no joke', along with trump-card treasures such as the one-use Heavenly Thunder Halberd; he clashes arrogantly with Zane and Randy in Eps 838+.
